verdict.rationale: Pipecat's core is a BSD-2 open-source Python framework. A runtime probe confirmed it pip-installs and imports with no key, and the docs say the same bot file is portable to most production self-hosting setups. Community reports add that local inference via ollama and local whisper STT is supported, so the stack can run fully self-hosted. missing for 10: a detailed first-party production self-hosting deployment guide (the built-in dev runner is explicitly not supported for production use).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: pypi pipecat-ai 1.8.1 (BSD-2 OSS) installs and `import pipecat` succeeds with no key, printing its startup banner — the open-source voice-agent framework is real, pip-installable, and self-hostable.
Open source Python framework for building voice and multimodal AI pipelines.
This is the property that makes the same bot file portable across the development runner, Pipecat Cloud, and most production self-hosting setups.
Local inference is already supported via Pipecat, you can use ollama or any custom OpenAI endpoint. Local STT is also supported via whisper, which pipecat will download and manage for you.
